Kurt Vile told Rolling Stone in September 2020 that he began listening to John Prine in his early twenties after a fan told him he sounded like Prine, and spent what he called "one cool summer" on the greatest hits.
Kurt Vile said in an interview with Under the Radar in April 2022 that he grew up listening to the Velvet Underground.

Kurt Vile told Under the Radar in April 2022 that signing to Matador was a lifelong dream because it was "home of Pavement, Yo La Tengo, Cat Power, so many people I grew up listening to"; Russh magazine reported in 2023 that his high-school idols were Pavement and Dinosaur Jr.
Kurt Vile named Yo La Tengo in the same Under the Radar quote about signing to Matador Records in April 2022.

Kurt Vile named Dinosaur Jr. among his high-school idols in a 2023 Russh interview, alongside Pavement; AllMusic's prose biography and Wikipedia's sourced influence line both describe him as taking notes from masters including Neil Young, Sonic Youth and Dinosaur Jr.

The same Uncut account names Nick Drake among the artists Lowell Brams introduced Sufjan Stevens to that summer; Stevens later covered Drake's "Pink Moon" for a 2021 single.

Sufjan Stevens told Uncut in February 2015 that there was no music, art or television at home growing up -- his stepfather Lowell Brams introduced him and his siblings to the Beatles, the Rolling Stones, Ry Cooder, Bob Dylan, Nick Drake and Frank Zappa the summer they moved to Eugene, an experience Stevens described as Brams opening a Pandora's box.

Far Out and Dazed both report Mark E. Smith telling Irmin Schmidt that Can "saved my life," recalling how he bought Tago Mago by mail order as a teenager and later phoned Schmidt directly to ask Can to play with The Fall.

Mark E. Smith named the Velvet Underground among the few artists he rated in the same conversation where he described Can's Tago Mago as formative, and told Crack Magazine he preferred the repetition of the Velvet Underground and Can to the Sex Pistols'.
